title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
authors: Lizhang Chen, Jonathan Li, Chen Liang, Ni Lao, Qiang Liu
gist: Re-runs a block of four layers in the middle of a released model at inference time, with no training. Plain repetition breaks the model, so each pass takes a damped fraction of the step the block was trained to make. Mixture-of-experts models loop one layer at a time so their expert choices stay fixed. The cache keeps one entry per layer, as in the original model.
changes: Shows depth can be a setting on a model already in service. More passes give more compute per token with the same weights and the same cache size, which opens lever 7. The gains are a point or two, and finding the block took a search per model and benchmark.
caveats: The abstract says there was no per-cell tuning, but an appendix describes a per-cell search over about 720 settings. Only the 30B check was fixed in advance, and it gained at most 1.1 points in a table that leaves out cells where both settings lost. No intervals. Looping every generated token cost 22% more time. The authors' code repository returned 404 on 22 November.

numbers.setup: best of a per-cell search; 5-shot chain of thought; H100

numbers.metric: Time per query, looping every generated token
numbers.setup: Qwen3-4B, 200 GSM8K questions, three sub-steps over 4 of 36 layers

bears_on.note: Depth can be added with no training and no growth in the cache, but the gain is a point or two for extra compute on every looped token.
